definition: A section of track that only one train may occupy at a time, guarded by a brake or lift at its exit.
The chain or cable slope that gives a coaster train its stored energy before the first drop.
A stretch of track with brakes that slows or stops a train, usually before the station.
The wheel that runs under the rail so a train cannot lift off the track.
Rocky Mountain Construction's flat-topped steel rail used to convert wooden coasters into hybrids.
Linear synchronous motor: track coils that push permanent magnets on the train to launch or brake it.
Linear induction motor: track coils that push a plain metal fin on the train by inducing currents in it.
A sled running between the rails that hooks a train and tows it during a hydraulic or pneumatic launch.
A pressure tank where hydraulic fluid compresses nitrogen gas to store launch energy.
The brake at the lip of a dive coaster's drop that pauses the train face-down before release.
A coaster layout that does not form a circuit; the train reverses and rides the same track backward.
A movable section of track that sends a train onto a different route mid-ride.
A continuous chain of swivelling pod vehicles that loads from a moving belt and never stops.
A battery-powered ride vehicle guided by floor markers or a buried wire instead of a rail.
A Disney ride vehicle with a motion base mounted on a slow, steerable chassis.
The number of independent ways a platform can move, up to six: surge, sway, heave, roll, pitch and yaw.
A six-legged hexapod that moves a platform in all six degrees of freedom.
Drifting a motion platform back to centre slower than riders can feel, so it is ready for the next cue.
Leaning a simulator seat slowly so gravity imitates a sustained acceleration.
A simulator whose seats are lifted into a dome screen with riders' feet hanging free.
A water-filled trough at the end of a track section that slows a boat on a flume or water coaster.
The landing of a water-ride boat into a pool that stops it and throws up a wave.
A contactless brake in which fins pass magnets and the induced currents slow the vehicle.
A monorail whose car wraps over the top of a single beam on rubber tyres.
A park's published scale, from gentle to aggressive, telling guests how intense a ride is.
One attraction that chains several ride technologies, such as a simulator, a trackless vehicle and a drop.
